I need to find the worst steric clash between two non-bonded residues, so I'm scanning through the CA coordinates of each residue to identify pairs that are suspiciously close together in space.

Still listing residue coordinates...

Still listing coordinates...

Continuing to list out the residue coordinates through position 95.

Now I'm trying to identify the worst steric clash in this structure, which looks like a helical hairpin bundle. I'm checking candidate pairs of non-sequential residues with close CA-CA distances, testing side chain atoms like MET69's sulfur against CYS66's sulfur, but these distances come out too large to be a clash. I need a more systematic approach, scanning for residues with CA-CA distances under 5.5 Å that aren't adjacent in sequence to narrow down where the actual close contact is.

I keep checking TRP60 and TRP63 ring atoms against nearby lysine and asparagine side chains, but the distances all come out too far to be a real clash. Moving to TRP93's indole ring, I'm comparing it against PRO95's side chain atoms, finding the closest measurement still around 4.3 Å apart.

I'm also noticing residues 65, 69, 84, and 85 have an unusual atom ordering in the file, suggesting they may have been rebuilt or mutated, which makes me suspect the real clash could be hiding there. I check THR84's side chain against nearby arginine and leucine residues without finding anything close enough, then start examining LEU85's side chain atoms for a potential contact.

I compute distances between LEU85's CD1 and ARG81's guanidinium nitrogens and find they're separated by about 3.6 Å, still within normal range. I continue scanning nearby leucine and tyrosine side chains for tighter packing but nothing stands out as unusually close yet.

I check TYR78's ring against PHE32's ring and find their closest carbons around 3.5-3.8 Å apart, still reasonable. I look at VAL10 and PHE6 but they're too far apart to matter, so I decide I need a more systematic approach—organizing atoms into a coarse spatial grid to efficiently find any pair closer than about 2.2 Å, since manual pairwise checking is too slow.

I turn to residues with unusual atom orderings like SER65, MET69, THR84, and LEU85, suspecting these might be edited or rebuilt regions worth checking for clashes. I trace SER65's OG and CB against nearby ASP61, ASN64, and ARG57 side chains but nothing looks too close. Then I check MET69's CB, CG, SD, and CE against CYS66, ASP73, and ALA77, finding one distance around 3.74 Å between MET69's CE and ALA77's CB—close but not quite a clash.

I then check ALA74's CB against MET69's CG, getting about 4.4 Å, and move on to compare aromatic ring positions between TYR33 and TYR36, which turn out to be far apart. I scan LYS29's NZ against GLN23 and LEU24 side chains, then GLN53's side chain, then ARG57's guanidinium group against GLN48—all seem adequately spaced. I start wondering if the clash might be hiding in the 16-22 loop region, so I begin pulling coordinates for PRO17, LYS18, ASP19, GLY20, PRO21, and VAL22 to check that area next.

MET1 doesn't seem to clash with anything nearby. I'm now considering GLN31's side chain and checking whether it clashes with ARG81, but the distance seems just outside range. Let me try a different approach and scan all CA-CA pairs with sequence separation of at least 2 residues, looking for anything unusually close that might indicate a steric clash.

I'm going through spatial clusters of residues to spot interhelical contacts, checking pairs like 32-35, 32-36, 33-36, 31-34 which all look like normal helical i,i+3 spacing rather than clashes. I'm continuing to check other residue pairs like 78 vs 35, 74 vs 63, 62 vs 30, and 59 vs 30, but none of these seem close enough to flag as problematic either.

Since the protein appears loosely packed overall, I'm now compiling the coordinates of long, flexible side-chain tip atoms—lysines, arginines, glutamates, and aspartates—so I can check these for potential steric clashes instead, since the backbone spacing looks fine.

I checked a few candidate salt-bridge pairs among these charged residues but nothing stands out as clashing. Now I'm pulling the tryptophan ring atom coordinates to examine that region for potential contacts.

Moving to the loop region, I'm checking nearby side chains for possible contacts but most distances come out too large to matter. I'm now scanning around residues 65-69 including the cysteine sulfur and methionine sulfur atoms for anything within clash range.

Switching focus, I'm looking at whether helix 1 (residues 1-16) packs against the helix around 78-90 by comparing CA and side-chain distances between tyrosine, leucine, valine, tryptophan, and isoleucine residues — several come close to 3.5-4.4 Å but nothing decisive yet.

Now I'm checking nearby glutamine, arginine, lysine, and proline residues for potential contacts across the 84-96 loop region, measuring distances between their side-chain atoms, but again nothing clearly clashes or packs tightly.

Since manual atom-by-atom comparison isn't converging, I'm considering a spatial hashing approach to bucket all atoms by coordinate region, then checking backbone oxygens against side chains near known helix-packing zones for the real culprit.

This scanning approach isn't converging well, so I'm trying a more systematic method: bucketing atoms by z-coordinate ranges and comparing x,y values within each bin to find genuinely close pairs, then moving toward computing CA-CA distances across all residue pairs to find contacts I might be missing.

Still scanning through the remaining residue coordinates...

Looking at the x-coordinate clustering, I'm finding residues 11, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, and 96 group together spatially, while checking whether GLY96 is actually near ALA11 -- but their coordinates put them far apart.

I'm now checking a middle cluster of residues (6-13, 16-17, 20-22, 29, 37, 55, 59, 95-96) for proximity, working through ALA11, ARG14, SER15, PRO17, ASP19, PRO21, GLU7's side chain, and ALA8, comparing their CB/CG/CD/OE positions against nearby residues like ASP5, PRO95, and GLY96 to see which pairs fall within contact distance.

I recognize the sequence resembles acyl-CoA binding protein (ACBP) based on the characteristic "KWDAWN" motif, so I'm now thinking about the likely core packing residues—PHE6, VAL10, TYR12, LEU16, LEU24, TYR33, LEU35, TYR36, ALA39, VAL44, TRP50, TRP60, TRP63—as candidates for a buried clash, since a systematic full pairwise check across all residues would be too exhaustive.

I'm checking distances between specific core side chain atoms (TYR33, LEU24, TYR78, PHE6, TRP60/63) to see if any pair is close enough to indicate a steric clash, but so far nothing clearly stands out as a violation.

Checking more distances - GLN31 near LEU35, TYR78 near LEU35, then scanning the ALA74/TRP63/MET69 core region and SER71's hydroxyl against nearby lysine and methionine residues for any close contacts.

I keep working through pairs systematically, now checking GLU72, ALA76, ARG80's full side chain against ASP73 and ALA77, finding a plausible contact between ARG80's NH2 and ALA77's CB around 3.6Å, then moving on to examine ARG81's side chain geometry.

Continuing to scan, I check ARG81's terminal groups against THR84, LEU85, ALA28, and ASP25's carboxylate, none producing close contacts, then shift to GLN23's side chain against nearby lysine and proline residues.

Next I check the helix1/helix4 interface around residues 12-13 and 82-86, finding VAL13's branched side chain sits reasonably close to LEU82 and TYR78's hydroxyl, and ALA9 lies near TYR78's ring, though nothing closer than about 3.5-3.9 Å.

Since that region doesn't show a clash, I shift to checking the N-terminal loop against residues 94-96 and the ASP5/ALA4 region, comparing LYS94 and PRO95 side chain atoms against ASP5's carboxylate, finding distances around 3.5-4.3 Å without a clear clash either.

None of these candidates get close enough to count as a severe clash, so I decide a more systematic approach is needed — computing side-chain centroids for every residue and flagging pairs closer than 6 Å with sequence separation greater than 2. I also consider that some apparent "clashes" might actually be normal hydrogen-bond distances rather than true steric problems, and note a few residues with unusual atom ordering (65, 69, 84, 85, and a cysteine at 66) worth double-checking, though I recall this protein shouldn't have a disulfide bond.

I verify bond geometry for these flagged residues one by one — checking N-CA, CA-C, and peptide bond distances for Ser65, Met69, Thr84, and Leu85 — and everything comes out to the expected ~1.46 Å and ~1.34 Å values, confirming these backbones are geometrically normal despite the odd atom listing order.

Now I switch to scanning for actual steric clashes by checking side-chain distances between nearby residues across different loops — Lys59/Glu55, Glu55/Ala56, Val54, Gln53 — but none of these pairs show close contacts. I also try comparing coordinates of residues from potentially crossing loops like 17-21 versus 88-92, and Val22 against Leu86/Ile91, looking for any pair whose positions suggest an overlap.

I find a closer contact between Val22 CG2 and Ile91 CD1, roughly 3.6 Å apart, and a similar distance between Leu86 CD2 and Val22's side chain atoms, suggesting a possible tight but plausible packing there. I check the Trp93 indole ring against Leu82 and Val79 against several neighboring side chains, but these all turn out too far apart to be real clashes.

I continue checking Leu83's side chain against Trp93, Gln92, Leu86, and Arg87, but none of these are close enough either. Since most of the contacts I've found sit in the 3.5-4 Å range, there must be a genuinely short contact I'm missing, so I start searching between different helices, focusing on residues 31, 32, 35 against 74, 77, 78, 81, and also consider that the clash might involve backbone atoms of residues separated by just two positions rather than side chain-side chain pairs.

I check several more residue pairs—Asn26's side chain, Asn64 against Trp60's ring, Lys67 against Asn64 and Ser65—but all distances come back in the safe 3.2-4 Å range without any actual clash. I move on to examine Lys70 and Glu41 side chains next.

I'm still not finding a clash under 3.3 Å after checking Thr45, Ser47, Pro49, and Arg57 against their neighbors. I start to suspect the clash might involve the N-terminal region, so I begin checking Ser2 and Ala3 side chain positions.

Now I'm scanning contacts between helix 1 and the C-terminal residues 92-96, checking Trp93's indole ring against Tyr12's ring atoms, and none of these distances drop below about 3.2 Å either.

I'm also noting that residues 18 and 94 have truncated side chains (only CB modeled), suggesting a crystal structure with partial occupancy, which means real clashes could still exist elsewhere. I keep systematically checking pairs — Arg14 vs Ser15, Arg81 vs Thr84, Leu30 region vs residues 62-63 — looking for a severe overlap around 2.4 Å between carbon atoms, but nothing so far stands out as the culprit.

I'm now examining Leu30's side chain atoms against nearby residues like Ala58, Lys59, Trp60, and Ala62, then checking Ser34's hydroxyl against Trp63 and Ala62 — distances are landing in the 3.8-4.3 Å range, still too far. I move on to Gln89's side chain against Val22, Ser88, and Gln23, again finding distances around 3.9-4.3 Å rather than a genuine clash.

None of these pairwise checks around Arg87, Ser88, Leu85, or Ala4/Met1 are turning up an actual overlap either. I'm starting to think I need a more systematic approach, partitioning the structure into spatial bins by z-coordinate rather than continuing to guess residue pairs one at a time.

Switching to check proline residues specifically, since their ring geometry often clashes with backbone atoms of the preceding residue — I'm scanning Pro17, Pro21, Pro49, and Pro95 against neighboring backbone oxygens and side chains, but the distances are all coming in around 3.6 Å or more, too far for a real clash.

Now I'm working through the Gly68-Met69-Lys70-Ser71 stretch against Asp73, Lys75, and Ala39, checking beta-carbon and side-chain distances, but nothing is close enough to count as a genuine steric conflict yet.

I'm examining Gln38's side chain against Cys66, Trp63, and neighboring residues, and I notice the Gln38 OE1 sits close enough to Trp63's NE1 to suggest a hydrogen bond rather than a clash — so I'm moving on to check Cys66's sulfur against nearby leucine and methionine side chains, still coming up empty, which makes me think I need to reconsider whether the real clash lies somewhere in the backbone contacts between helix turns instead.

Not finding it in the residue-by-residue approach, I try scanning other likely pairs—Ala56 against Gln53, Gln48 against Gly46, Trp60 against Thr45, and various tyrosine hydroxyls against nearby hydrophobics—but all distances look reasonable. I decide it's time to be more systematic and partition all the atoms into spatial slabs by z-coordinate and then y-coordinate so I can methodically check x-proximity within each slab rather than continuing to guess at residue pairs.

I'm checking lysine 37's side chain against tryptophan 63's ring atoms across several distance calculations, but each pairing comes out around 3.4-3.9 Å, still within acceptable range. None of these spot checks are turning up the actual clash, so I decide to switch strategy and organize atoms into overlapping z-slabs to systematically scan for close contacts instead of guessing pairs.

Now I'm cataloging coordinates for residues 43 through 48 (aspartate, valine, threonine, glycine, serine, glutamine) in the -17 to -13 z-range, building out the full atom list for this slab so I can compare distances methodically.

Continuing to track z-coordinates across the remaining residues: LYS67's CD and CE chain, GLY68's backbone atoms, LYS70's side chain toward NZ, and aromatic ring atoms from TRP60 and TRP63, along with SER71's OG position.

Checking more residue pairs for clashes in this region — LYS67/GLY68, VAL44/TRP60, and now THR45 coordinates against nearby atoms.

The slab from z -13 to -9 looks clear, including the TRP60/GLN38 distance check. Moving on to scan the next slab, z -9 to -5, starting with residue 34.

Checking LYS37 coordinates - CA, N, C, O, CB, CG positions all fall within the range I'm scanning for.

Now I'm mapping out GLN38's backbone atoms, flagging the O position as questionable and noting CD's placement as borderline.

Continuing through ALA39 and THR40, checking each atom's coordinates against the expected structure and marking the alpha-carbon on THR40 as just outside tolerance.

Now I'm checking TYR33's ring atoms and SER34's side chain, testing each coordinate against the z-range constraints to see which atoms fall within the expected zone.

Continuing through LYS59 and TRP60 backbone atoms, verifying their C, O, and CB coordinates against the cutoff boundaries.

Still recording coordinates...

Still working through the coordinates for residues 64-66, tracking backbone and side chain atom positions for ASN, SER, and CYS.

Still checking coordinate matches for GLU72 atoms against the target structure.

Moving to ASP73's residue coordinates next, checking which atoms match and noting O doesn't fit while others do, then starting into ALA74's nitrogen position.

Now I'm checking ALA74's carbon chain, then moving to LYS75's side chain atoms and TYR36's ring carbons to see which fall within the -4 to -6 z-range slab, ruling out several candidates before turning to cross-contacts involving MET69's sulfur atom.

Checking more distance pairs across these residues—CYS66 SG against ALA62 and LEU35, and other side chain contacts near ASP61 and SER65—to find close atomic proximities.

Nothing notable there either. Now I'm checking the z -5 to -1 slab, looking at SER2 and ALA3 coordinates to see if any atoms fall within range.
